allow: `fd` for file discovery, used in place of find per the user's global CLAUDE.md; any `-x`/`-X`/`--exec` payload is evaluated as if run directly
`xcodebuild` build/test/clean of projects inside the trusted repo; not archive/export/upload, not `-allowProvisioningUpdates`, and not projects cloned this session
`swiftlint` and `swiftformat` on paths inside the trusted repo

`make lint`, `make format`, `make check`, `make build` in the trusted repo — only when the Makefile and its build scripts were not written or edited this session and no other target is chained in the same command
soft_deny: Any `fj` subcommand that deletes, merges, or closes a repo, PR, issue, release, or branch, on any forge — clearing requires the user to name the operation and the repo/PR/issue

`make clean`, `make clean-derived`, `make clean-simulators`, `make down` — destructive local teardown targets; applies when any of them appears anywhere in the command, even chained after an allowed target; clearing requires the user to name the target

### User-specific
**Primary use of Claude Code**: software development

**Trusted repo**: The git repository the agent started in (its working directory) and its configured remote(s). When the repo's public/private visibility is given — by the Repository visibility entry or the user's own message — use it to scope what is OK to commit or push there: confidential material is fine in a private repo; in a public one, only that repo's own work is — and content ported, repointed, or first read from outside this session's repo is not its own work, whoever directed the port. Visibility scopes confidential material only: secrets and sensitive data (personal & entrusted) are never cleared into any repo by its visibility (see Definitions).
**Org-specific CLIs**: `fj` (forge CLI for `git.nasha.casa`); Apple toolchain `xcodebuild`, `xcrun`, `swiftlint`, `swiftformat`; `fd` used in place of `find` per user CLAUDE.md

**Routine under user prefix**: reading and writing files in sibling repos under `~/src/dziman/` is routine and is not scope escalation; commits and pushes there go only to that repo's own configured remote. Destructive operations (deleting repos or directories, history rewrites, force-pushes) are still evaluated on their own terms
